simple.meaning: מָן (mân) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “literally a whatness (so to speak), i.e. manna (so called from the question about it).” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 14 times across Exodus, Numbers, Deuteronomy, Joshua, Nehemiah, and 1 more, beginning at Exodus 16:15. Its contexts include land, Israel.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to מָן (H4478).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.

occurrences.englishText: When the children of Israel saw it, they said to one another, “What is it?” For they didn’t know what it was. Moses said to them, “It is the bread which Yahweh has given you to eat.
The house of Israel called its name “Manna”,† “Manna” means “What is it?” and it was like coriander seed, white; and its taste was like wafers with honey.
Moses said to Aaron, “Take a pot, and put an omer-full of manna in it, and lay it up before Yahweh, to be kept throughout your generations.”
The children of Israel ate the manna forty years, until they came to an inhabited land. They ate the manna until they came to the borders of the land of Canaan.

but now we have lost our appetite. There is nothing at all except this manna to look at.”
The manna was like coriander seed, and it looked like bdellium.† Bdellium is a resin extracted from certain African trees.
When the dew fell on the camp in the night, the manna fell on it.

He humbled you, allowed you to be hungry, and fed you with manna, which you didn’t know, neither did your fathers know, that he might teach you that man does not live by bread only, but man lives by every word that proceeds out of Yahweh’s mouth.
who fed you in the wilderness with manna, which your fathers didn’t know, that he might humble you, and that he might prove you, to do you good at your latter end;
The manna ceased on the next day, after they had eaten of the produce of the land. The children of Israel didn’t have manna any more, but they ate of the fruit of the land of Canaan that year.
